label: C30-localized-mild-update
patientMessage: I recommend self-care at home with over-the-counter measures from your pharmacist for this poison ivy rash. It is limited to your forearms, the itch is mild, and you report no fever or breathing trouble, so no clinician assessment is needed right now. If you develop fever, increasing pain, pus, or rash on your face, eyes or genitals, get clinician assessment the same day; Counsel can help coordinate, but go to an urgent care or your own doctor if same-day review isn't secured — don't wait for a reply here. Seek emergency care for trouble breathing or facial/throat swelling.
reason: Localized, mildly itchy vesicular rash confined to both forearms after known poison ivy exposure, with no fever, no breathing trouble, no face/eye/genital involvement and no increasing pain or pus reported; no decision-critical clinician task is established, so guidance plus an action-based safety net is sufficient.

criteria.reason: Mild localized rash supports guidance without required assessment.
